pr_title: Expose min/max attributes on plant integration

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Fixes https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/70583

The min/max values that the `plant` component uses to make calculations are not exposed as attributes.  This causes problems for custom cards such as the [Lovelace Flower Card](https://github.com/Olen/lovelace-flower-card), as users must used a [patched version](https://github.com/Olen/homeassistant-plant) of this component.

This change exposes those values under the `limits` section within the attributes.

pr_comments:
Hi @greghesp, 

It seems you haven't yet signed a CLA. Please do so [here](https://home-assistant.io/developers/cla_sign_start/?pr=home-assistant/core#71514).

Once you do that we will be able to review and accept this pull request.

Thanks!

> Why not putting the `min/max` at the root level ?
> 
> ```yaml
> max_brightness: 60000
> max_conductivity: 2000
> max_moisture: 75
> max_temperature: 35
> min_brightness: 3000
> min_conductivity: 425
> min_moisture: 16
> min_temperature: 8
> ```
> 
> instead of
> 
> ```yaml
> limits:
>     max_brightness: 60000
>     max_conductivity: 2000
>     max_moisture: 75
>     max_temperature: 35
>     min_brightness: 3000
>     min_conductivity: 425
>     min_moisture: 16
>     min_temperature: 8
> ```
> 
> For example, for lights the `max_mired/min_mired` is at the root level
> 
> ```yaml
> min_mireds: 153
> max_mireds: 588
> ```
> 
> Also, I think it can be good to populate the `min/max` with the default values if it's not provided in the options to always have access to this attributes from the front-end for example.

I put them within limits, as HA already has some attributes called `max_`.  For example, it exposes a `max_brightness` attribute at the root level, but this is used by the integration from the [maximum value based off the attributes history](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/71514/files#diff-6b9ddf54e1eedbef6fc656a75bba49fbee6626abd31ce4e335a199479bbaeb7cL358)

The default values should always be exposed with this PR, and then overwritten if they are [passed through the configuration](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/71514/files#diff-6b9ddf54e1eedbef6fc656a75bba49fbee6626abd31ce4e335a199479bbaeb7cR96)
Ok, I didn't see the default fallback in config 😅

There hasn't been any activity on this pull request recently. This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because of that and will be closed if no further activity occurs within 7 days.
Thank you for your contributions.

issue_context.title: Min/Max values on Plant integration not populated as attributes
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Providing the `min_xxxx` values in the `plant` configuration, do not load as attributes for the entity.  If this is not a bug, please consider exposing these values, as it prevents any type of useful custom card without using the [patched plant](https://github.com/Olen/homeassistant-plant) component

Would be great if these could be exposed as a dict under `limits` in the attributes

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.4.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Plant

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/plant

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
plant:
  Tulip:
    sensors:
      moisture: sensor.plant_moisture
      battery: sensor.plant_battery
      temperature: sensor.plant_temperature
      conductivity: sensor.plant_conductivity
      brightness: sensor.plant_brightness
    min_moisture: 15
    max_moisture: 60
    min_temperature: 6
    max_temperature: 35
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?


review_comments:
These add static attributes that are stored in our state machine (and thus add memory usage and cost storage space in database history recording), while their only use is a custom UI card.

I suggest on making this configurable on the card configuration instead in such cases.

I suggested to expose theses attributes values like the `mired_min/mired_max` for light for example (or the min max values for climate entity) to avoid the user to enter the value twice (in the integration and in the card).
Also, there is default value and user has no idea about these default value unless he go to the documentation.

But I understand your arguments about database performance for static information.

I will look how we can deal with it in lovelace card. Adding 8 input number looks a little overloaded 😅

> I suggested to expose theses attributes values like the mired_min/mired_max for light for example (or the min max values for climate entity) 

That is not comparable, as those can be provided by an integration (e.g., the device on the Zigbee network or whatever else).

This is static manual configuration.

Also, I don't know the status of the plant domain in the HA core codebase. It's `yaml` only, there is few commits on it and it looks like a helper but very specific. Maybe it can be migrated to a sensor helper like the utility meter or it's better to use template sensor for these rules.

> Also, I don't know the status of this plant entity in the HA core codebase.

I don't know either. There is no state at this point. As a helper it might work; however, in the end, I think this platform, in general, isn't providing anything really.

For example, its state is "problem" or "OK", ergo: A binary state. It should be a binary sensor entity, not a `plant` entity. We have a couple of more of these occurrences (e.g., promixity; which should be just a sensor actually).

I think in the long-term, the chances are pretty high that we convert these into their proper entity types. As for `plant` itself, I'm not sure if a dedicated entity would be even warranted. It is merely used as a frontend thing and for automations using all original sensor entities, in general, would be easier to automate with/on (including their min/max values); it would be more consistent with all other stuff we have as well.

Totally agree 👍 I think that a binary_sensor with a proper device_class should be cleaner 🙂

Note that `utility_meter` sensors expose config values but it's just to tease you 🤪

e.g.
```yaml
meter_period: daily
cron pattern: 0 0 * * *
```

> Note that utility_meter sensors expose config values but it's just to tease you

More stuff like that is still there, however, we do try to minimize it nowadays. Things from the past we did a lot and learned from 😉
The custom UI card is not the only use though. I have wanted to have those states available for automation scopes (mainly notifications), so would appreciate to be allowed for!

> I have wanted to have those states available for automation scopes (mainly notifications), so would appreciate to be allowed for!

The point made above, is that those are not states; they are configurations.

> 
> The point made above, is that those are not states; they are configurations.

Sorry, yes I understand. Point however is that it is useful to have these configurations available somehow to use in automations in addition to the UI cards.
Sure, but they are not state, thus don't belong in the state engine 🤷
